verses.text: It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and such sexual immorality as is not even named among the Gentiles, that one has his father’s wife.
You are puffed up, and didn’t rather mourn, that he who had done this deed might be removed from among you.
For I most certainly, as being absent in body but present in spirit, have already, as though I were present, judged him who has done this thing.
In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, you being gathered together, and my spirit, with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ,
are to deliver such a one to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.
Your boasting is not good. Don’t you know that a little yeast leavens the whole lump?
Purge out the old yeast, that you may be a new lump, even as you are unleavened. For indeed Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed in our place.
Therefore let us keep the feast, not with old yeast, neither with the yeast of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
I wrote to you in my letter to have no company with sexual sinners;
yet not at all meaning with the sexual sinners of this world, or with the covetous and extortionists, or with idolaters; for then you would have to leave the world.

But as it is, I wrote to you not to associate with anyone who is called a brother who is a sexual sinner, or covetous, or an idolater, or a slanderer, or a drunkard, or an extortionist. Don’t even eat with such a person.
For what do I have to do with also judging those who are outside? Don’t you judge those who are within?
But those who are outside, God judges. “Put away the wicked man from among yourselves.”

footnotes.content: When word of sin travels fast through a congregation, Paul doesn't pretend it hasn't happened. He speaks plainly, as one who loves the church too much for silence. The Lord sees all and calls us to honest reckoning, not comfortable blindness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Pride can dress itself in many robes—including pride in our own liberty or tolerance. Paul reminds them: there's a time for mourning over sin, not boasting around it. The church's health matters more than any one person's comfort.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Distance doesn't separate Paul from his flock—his spirit is with them. When a congregation's shepherd cannot be there in body, the Spirit carries him near. What matters most is the Lord's presence and wisdom, not the chair we sit in.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The church gathered is Christ's body—and His power stands with them. When believers come together in His name to act, they do not act alone. This is the weight and glory of church discipline: it's carried in His authority, not our own anger.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even in judgment there is mercy. Paul speaks of handing over to Satan—not out of vindictiveness, but that the flesh might die so the spirit might be saved. The Lord's goal in every discipline is healing, not simply punishment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A little yeast works through the whole loaf—so small a thing, yet so pervasive. I've watched how one unchecked sin in a family or a church can color everything, slowly and almost invisibly. Humility means paying attention to what others might overlook.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Christ is our Passover—once sacrificed, His blood marks us forever. Just as Israel purged out old yeast to remember their deliverance, we purge out what corrupts so we remember Christ's sacrifice. Holiness and gratitude belong together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: To keep feast with Christ is to live in sincerity and truth—not the theatrical piety that hides our hearts. He asks not for perfection but for honesty, for the unleavened bread of a conscience that doesn't deceive itself or others.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul has written before about separation—and now he must clarify, because the world loves to misunderstand what holiness costs. Believers must distinguish themselves from sin, yes, but not from sinners. That's where the discernment lives.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If the church cut off every conversation with the wicked world, we'd have to leave this world altogether. But we're sent into it as Christ's witnesses, living among those who don't yet know Him. Separation from sin doesn't mean fleeing from sinners.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A brother or sister who names the Lord yet lives in unrepented sin is different—they've tasted His grace and turned from it. Paul says even the table of fellowship must wait until they turn back. It's not hatred; it's the language of love that won't pretend.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The church judges its own; the world's judgment belongs to God alone. I've watched believers waste years trying to reform the whole world while their own household suffers. Wisdom knows where our jurisdiction lies and rests gladly in the rest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in these words: the church still carries the hard duty of naming sin and sometimes of separation. We live it imperfectly, stumbling between judgment and grace. Yet Christ remains the shepherd, and His standard never shifts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
